title: Intrinsic finite-coefficient bounds descend from binary local models
statement: Let Z be a Noetherian scheme, U,V open subsets with U union V=Z, A a finite commutative ring, and a,b,s,t integers. In the ordinary unbounded constant-ring module derived category let K be on Z, P on U and Q on V. Assume specified derived isomorphisms from the canonical constant-ring inverse images of K to P and Q. Suppose each of P and Q has homology zero in every degree i<a or b<i, HasProEtaleTorAmplitude in [s,t] [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], and, in each degree, intrinsically constructible fixed-module homology after applying the derived inverse of sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Then K has these same three properties with the unchanged intervals. This is a finite-level assertion for any existing K and any finite ring A: it constructs no global object, uses no tower or overlap isomorphism, and asserts no distinguished triangle.

proof.text: Identify fixed-module constructibility with finite constant models. In one direction use finite_models_of_fixed_lisse on every stratum; in the other use finiteModels_over and finite_geometricStalk_of_finite_models. If there are zero strata, the scheme is empty; use the positive one-stratum identity partition and the empty trivializing cover. The module-sheafification unit identifies every fixed-module sheaf F with restriction to constant scalars of its intrinsic realization. Apply this to the inverse realization of intrinsic homology and compose with the realization counit. Exactness commutes with homology, so the fixed-module hypothesis of the item is equivalent to intrinsic constructibility of each homology object.

source.place: Tags 09AJ, 093I and 099Y; finite stratifications and constant coefficient realization

proof.text: Compare derivedTensor for any allowed K-flat resolution with the native localization tensor via RingedDerivedNative.tensorIso. The resolution quasi-isomorphism identifies its first tensor factor with the chosen derived object. The singleFunctorIsoCompQ comparison identifies the second factor with the degree-zero test module. Applying the same comparison to proEtaleDerivedTensor proves that HasProEtaleTorAmplitude is exactly the ordered interval together with vanishing of the chosen tensors against every module sheaf. This proves both directions, so the final result retains the original all-representatives, all-resolutions predicate.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 08FZ; independence of resolutions and the degree-zero module test

proof.text: Index the two opens by Fin 2. Transport intrinsic constructibility, homology vanishing and Tor amplitude along the supplied local-model isomorphisms. The local cohomological supports lie in the finite integer interval [a,b], including when a>b (then the interval is empty). The cover equality supplies the jointly surjective family of open immersions. Apply finiteCoverCTFLocality with the ordered Tor interval [s,t] to get intrinsic constructibility of global homology and the global chosen-tensor vanishing in exactly that interval. The previous comparisons give the fixed-module constructibility and the original Tor predicate.

Retain the separate cohomological interval [a,b], rather than the possibly different Tor interval. For i<a or b<i, exact intrinsic pullback identifies the restriction of H^i(K) with homology of each local model, hence both restrictions vanish. Restriction to constant scalars commutes with these pullbacks. The proved open-cover zero-detection theorem makes the fixed-module encoding of H^i(K) zero, and the fully faithful encoding reflects this. Thus global homology vanishes in every requested degree.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 08FZ; exact restriction and covering-family zero detection

theorem proEtale_binary_ctf_of_local_models
    (Z : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian Z] (U V : Z.Opens) (_hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (a b s t : ℤ)
    (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory Z A)
    (P : proEtaleDerivedCategory U.toScheme A)
    (Q : proEtaleDerivedCategory V.toScheme A)
    (_aU : (proEtaleConstantRingDerivedPullback.{u} A U.ι).obj K ≅ P)
    (_aV : (proEtaleConstantRingDerivedPullback.{u} A V.ι).obj K ≅ Q)
    (_hP : (∀ i : ℤ, IsConstructibleProEtaleFixedModuleSheaf U.toScheme
      (ULift.{u + 1} A) ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 2} _ i).obj
        ((Functor.mapDerivedCategory.{u + 2, u + 1}
          (sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence.{u} U.toScheme A).inverse).obj P))) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{u + 2, u + 1, u + 2} _ i).obj P)) ∧
      HasProEtaleTorAmplitude U.toScheme A P s t)
    (_hQ : (∀ i : ℤ, IsConstructibleProEtaleFixedModuleSheaf V.toScheme
      (ULift.{u + 1} A) ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 2} _ i).obj
        ((Functor.mapDerivedCategory.{u + 2, u + 1}
          (sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence.{u} V.toScheme A).inverse).obj Q))) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{u + 2, u + 1, u + 2} _ i).obj Q)) ∧
      HasProEtaleTorAmplitude V.toScheme A Q s t) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, IsConstructibleProEtaleFixedModuleSheaf Z (ULift.{u + 1} A)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 2} _ i).obj
        ((Functor.mapDerivedCategory.{u + 2, u + 1}
          (sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence.{u} Z A).inverse).obj K))) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{u + 2, u + 1, u + 2} _ i).obj K)) ∧
      HasProEtaleTorAmplitude Z A K s t
